_comment: Shard definitions for test projects too large to run as a single unit.
A package listed here has its test suite split into shards; a package that
is not listed runs as one unit. Shards are crossed with the tier filters
(deterministic / coyote / chaos) by plan-test-matrix.py, so a shard is a
slice of a project's tests and a tier is a slice of a shard.
ORDERED FIRST-MATCH-WINS. Shards are evaluated top to bottom and a test
belongs to the FIRST shard whose include prefixes match it. The generated
filter for shard i is therefore OR(its own includes) AND NOT(includes of
every earlier shard). This is what makes the list a PARTITION rather than
an allow-list: every test lands in exactly one shard, so a suite cannot
silently lose coverage to a gap between two patterns, and two shards
cannot both claim the same test and run it twice.
The ordering is load-bearing. 'BPlusTree.ChaosPredicate' must precede
'BPlusTree.Chaos', which must precede 'BPlusTree.', because each is a
prefix of the one before it. Put a broad prefix above a narrow one and the
narrow shard silently runs nothing - which is why the leg summary reports
the executed test count per shard and the aggregate report flags any shard
that ran zero tests in every tier.
The final shard must set "complement": true. It matches everything no
earlier shard claimed, so adding a new test namespace can never fall
outside the partition and go untested.
Prefixes are relative to namespaceRoot and are matched against the VSTest
FullyQualifiedName, which is Namespace.Class.Method. A trailing dot pins
the match to a namespace segment ('Grains.'); no trailing dot lets it
match a class-name prefix ('ChaosPredicate'), which is how the chaos
fixtures that all share one namespace are split.
